question.problem: A triangle has sides $x$, $y$, and $z.$ The sides $x$ and $z$ have lengths $3$ and $4$, respectively. If the angle $Y$ between $x$ and $z$ has a measure of ${139}^{∘}$, what is the length of side $y?$ Round your answer to two decimal places.
question.worked_solution:
The following triangle illustrates the information given.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14269732/assets/7eaca5e621843857786ceda924f110804482d490c9dcd2615c6b3e50b89cde8e.png)

The Law of Cosines states that

$$
{y}^{2}={x}^{2}+{z}^{2}-2xz\operatorname{cos}⁡Y,
$$

Here, we have

$$
m∠Y={139}^{∘},\,x=3,\,z=4.
$$

Substituting the numbers into the formula gives

$$
\begin{aligned}{y}^{2} & ={3}^{2}+{4}^{2}-2(3)(4)\operatorname{cos}⁡{139}^{∘} \\  & =9+16-24\operatorname{cos}⁡{139}^{∘} \\  & =25-24(-0.754\,70…) \\  & =25+18.113\,03 \\  & =43.113\,03\end{aligned}
$$

rounded to $5$ decimal places. 

Taking the square root gives

$$
y=\sqrt{43.113\,03}=6.57
$$

rounded to two decimal places.
